subject: QuantRail discovery: model fit recommendations, evals, and fallback safeguards
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@quantrail.com>, Evan Soto <evan@quantrail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: QuantRail discovery: initial fit summary + immediate next steps

Hi Lisa / Evan —

Thanks again for today’s call. Quick recap and suggested path forward so we don’t lose momentum: 

- Observations from the session: your primary flows are structured ticket summarization (short form) and downstream entity normalization (high precision). Latency SLO target: 200–300ms p95 for 256-token tails.
- Shortlist of candidate families: llama-3-small/med variants (quantized), and an instruction-tuned open LLM (we referenced vicuna-8b variants in the call).
- Risk area noted: your production system currently runs nightly model updates — that raises quality-regression risk if a model binary is replaced without pinning.

Immediate next steps we recommend: 
1) I’ll send an evaluation pack with benchmark links, a prompt-set we used for your demo, and a short guide on pinning/rollback procedures (helps procurement and SRE).
2) Ben will follow up with a pricing snapshot for a dedicated mid-tier pool that meets your throughput needs.
3) Marissa will scope a short-run QA eval (50k tokens) to validate entity normalization precision.

Deliverables ETA: eval pack + benchmarking links by Wed 23 Jun. Can you confirm who on your side should get the detailed benchmark artifacts (procurement or SRE)?

Best,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments referenced: quantrail_call_notes.txt (see Drive link)

Thanks Hannah — that summary is spot on. Evan (cc'd) will own the SRE review but looped procurement here so they know an eval pack is coming. Please send everything to procurement@quantrail.com and myself.

One quick ask up front: our compliance team requires an explicit fallback plan if a model update degrades results. Would love a short doc we can attach to our vendor questionnaire that explains pinning and emergency rollback options.

Lisa Park

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: QuantRail Procurement <procurement@quantrail.com>, Lisa Park <lisa@quantrail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 16:20:00 -0400
Subject: Eval pack: benchmarks, prompts, recommended pins + safeguards (QuantRail)

Lisa / Procurement —

Attached is the eval pack we discussed. Summary highlights are below and the full artifacts are in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Qx-QuantRail-eval

Summary: 
- Benchmarks: we ran your sample dataset (~12k ticket threads) against three variants. See benchmark_summary_20270625.pdf for P95 latency and precision/recall tables.
  - Model A: redwood-llama3-med-q4 — best latency/throughput tradeoff (p95 220ms, entity F1 0.87)
  - Model B: open-vicuna-8b-qt — better precision on edge cases (F1 0.90) but 30% higher token cost
  - Model C: redwood-instruct-7b — safest for instruction-following prompts (slightly lower recall)

- Prompts: included prompt set file quantrail_eval_prompts_v1.csv (structured + free-text examples) mapped to each model variant.
- Pinning guidance: pinning_runbook.md gives the exact flags to pin a model version in Redwood Private/Dedicated, and the emergency rollback commands we recommend.

Risk & recommended guardrails: 
1) Enable per-route model pinning for your ticket-normalization route in Staging and Prod.
2) Add a lightweight evaluation hook that runs the 250-case prompt shard on every deploy (we can enable this as part of a canary).
3) Configure automatic fallback to Model B if Model A's entity F1 drops >4% relative to the pinned baseline.

Attachments (stubs): benchmark_summary_20270625.pdf (pdf), quantrail_eval_prompts_v1.csv (csv), pinning_runbook.md (md)

Next steps: 
- Ben will send price estimates for a two-month dedicated commit by Friday.
- Marissa: please propose a QA scope and timing for the 50k-token run.

Happy to hop on a short follow-up with Evan and procurement to walk through the runbook.

Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0400
Subject: Pricing snapshot & next steps (QuantRail commit options)

Lisa / team —

Per Hannah's request, attached is a short pricing snapshot for a mid-tier dedicated pool sized for your projected steady-state throughput. Key points: 
- 2-month commit (recommended for pilot): $34,000 — includes SLO-backed p95 target and 24/7 support during onboarding.
- Optional rollback support add-on: $4,500/mo (provides 24h exec on-call and priority patching for emergency pin/rollback).

If procurement wants to start with an MSA redline, send it over and we’ll loop legal. Deal details: HubSpot QR-2027-052.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing_snapshot_QR-2027-052.xlsx (stub)

From: Lisa Park <lisa@quantrail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Soto <evan@quantrail.com>, QuantRail Procurement <procurement@quantrail.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Eval pack: benchmarks, prompts, recommended pins + safeguards (QuantRail)

Team —

Quick update from our side: we ran the eval pack in staging and saw a surprising dip after a routine model binary refresh on Friday afternoon. Model A (redwood-llama3-med-q4) dropped to F1 0.82 on entity normalization for a subset of edge prompts (examples included). I’ve attached the failing prompt examples and a short diff of outputs.

This triggers our concern about automated nightly updates — we need the emergency rollback/playbook to be operational before we enable automated refreshes. Can Redwood confirm you can: 
1) Provide an emergency pin (to last-known-good) that we can apply from our side near-instantly?
2) Hold the auto-update for our production route until we complete a two-week validation window?

Happy to set a 30-min call today if easier.

Thanks,
Lisa

Attachments: failing_prompts_2906.csv, output_diffs_2906.txt

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Park <lisa@quantrail.com>, Evan Soto <evan@quantrail.com>, procurement@quantrail.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Eval pack: benchmarks, prompts, recommended pins + safeguards (QuantRail)

Ben / Marissa — heads up, QuantRail saw a regression during a routine refresh and needs immediate fallback/pinning support. They requested: emergency pin to last-known-good and a hold on auto-updates for prod.

Proposed internal plan (fast):
- Marissa: trigger the emergency pinning runbook (pin id: QR-2027-052-BASELINE) and confirm the version hash back to QuantRail (ETA 30m).
- Ben: confirm pricing add-on acceptance in case they want rollback support (procurement thread).
- Hannah: schedule a 30-min troubleshooting/call with Lisa & Evan, and provide a reproducible evaluation shard with failing prompts (I’ll upload examples to the Drive folder).

I’ll loop in Support after we confirm the pin. Marissa — can you acknowledge?

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
